title: Caldo Verde
subtitle: Portuguese kale and chorizo soup
excerpt: Portugal's most beloved soup: a simple, silky broth of potato thickened by blending into the liquid, enriched with olive oil, and finished with thin ribbons of kale and slices of chouriço. Simple, deeply sustaining, and one of the great soups of the world.

recipe.sourceNotes: Caldo verde (green broth) is considered the national soup of Portugal, originating in the Minho region of northern Portugal and eaten across the country at every occasion from weekday supper to wedding feast. The dish is built on a paradox: the most refined soups are often the simplest, and caldo verde contains almost nothing except potato, kale, olive oil, and sausage, yet the result is deeply satisfying and complex. The potato is cooked in water and then blended to create a silky, thickened broth; the olive oil is added generously at the end to give the soup its characteristic richness. The green element is couve galega, a type of Portuguese kale with very long, thin leaves; cavolo nero or curly kale are the best substitutes. The kale is sliced into the finest possible ribbons and added to the hot soup for just 3 to 5 minutes so it retains its colour. Chouriço is sliced into rounds and either fried separately or added to cook in the soup.

content.text: Cut the kale into the thinnest possible ribbons, almost a chiffonade: thick strips give a rough, tough result. The kale needs only 3 to 5 minutes in the hot soup; it should remain bright green. Blend the potato base until completely smooth. A hand blender in the pot is easier than transferring hot liquid.

items.preparation: stalks removed, leaves sliced into very fine ribbons
added at the end; plus extra to serve

content.text: Put the potato, onion, and garlic in a large pot. Cover with 1.5 litres of cold water. Add 1 teaspoon of salt. Bring to the boil and cook for 20 minutes until the potato is completely tender. Remove from the heat and blend until completely smooth with a hand blender. Return to the heat.
Fry the chorizo slices in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes per side until lightly crisped and the fat has rendered. Set aside.

Bring the potato broth to a simmer. Add the kale ribbons and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until just wilted and tender but still bright green. Add the olive oil and remaining salt and pepper. Stir. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Ladle into bowls and top with chorizo slices and an additional drizzle of olive oil.
